approval.review: Recorded for #246. This approval comes from the pstack interrogate panel under the owner's delegation of 2026-10-15, not from the owner. Changes from the #234 approval: native is upstream's from-source build of 10.12.0, source 928de8ff918488749ca9d23e0a7349873401b7f7, the Linux x86-64 executable 7b3c74db2c4ce06d2b483813a05c6b5928f81b10c471366d677ec25371b52693 carried by its published target image (pinned below), replacing 10.10.0's fd5ffef2d825d9035b3956b0026911a22e2c1b56f7fa205dd00310cfe88aeff5; restic is unchanged; the uniform runtime is Claude Code 2.1.276 through the gateway provider with claude-opus-5-5 at medium effort, replacing Codex 0.155.0 on Node.js v24.21.0 with gpt-5.6-sol, as the adopted environment dotnet-r6 (manifest SHA-256 304a417ca752e22652b66f3de47a5995247a45339ccd9fad8221f8f0b29fb89b) carries it, with the managed settings /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json (SHA-256 a469a57a1f61686f006df05d41973208f0bd9f81de219db17f4034882b038f2e), the only entry in /etc/claude-code, which turn off nonessential traffic and commit and PR attribution, pin effort to medium, output to 32000 tokens and CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY to {}, restrict requested models to claude-opus-5-5 (a session asked for a refused model falls back to claude-opus-5[1m] with a warning), turn off the advisor tool, background tasks and Workflows, skip WebFetch's preflight, deny WebFetch and WebSearch, and allow no hooks or MCP servers except managed ones, of which the file defines none; the gateway is sub2api at https://gateway.ai.faviann.com, replacing https://cliproxy.local.faviann.com/v1; and native 10.12.0's software-change graph has four executable nodes instead of six. Routing, read from the asset bytes because describe.py does not encode it: deliver runs only when the acceptance and code verdicts are both accepted; any other verdict pair goes to review_retry, and a ci_failed, conflict or repair_required delivery signal goes to delivery_retry; each is a map over the empty continueItems, so it ends the change iteration and the loop continues, and the next iteration runs the one worker node with that phase and its feedback, then both reviews and delivery again, for at most 10 iterations; a crash of either review is retried once in a new session (attempts 2), and a second crash fails the run; a crash of the worker or deliver, and a malformed, refusal or timeout error of any node, fails the run. Verified: generate.sh, unchanged from #234 and run with that executable copied out of the pinned image, produces these asset bytes twice in clean environments and native admits them with an exact round trip; describe.py, unchanged, reads the structure below (the worker, acceptance, code and deliver nodes, builtin.git-delivery.pr@2 with the v2/pr receipt (ready, ci_failed, conflict, repair_required) whose non-ready outcomes route to delivery_retry, the 10-iteration change loop, no node deadlines, gateway connections on every agent node, GH_TOKEN only on delivery, and the default consider pull-request feedback); a gateway probe on 2026-10-16 sent the bundled proposer's current request body (max_tokens 12000, reasoning_effort medium, the read_reference tool and the json_object format) and received a read_reference call and then a JSON proposal, and a probe on 2026-10-15 ran Claude Code with --json-schema through the gateway and received structured output; and an offline capture on the published dotnet-r6 image, with no proxy and every DNS query, TLS request and loopback connection logged, ran native 10.12.0's hosted lane on this asset three times (deliver's github connection removed, so each ended delivery_failed by design: once with the worker calling Bash, Edit and Write, asking Agent for haiku and writing CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY with effort max, 64000 tokens and speed fast into .claude/settings.json before both reviewers ran, once with every node asking Agent for fable, and once with every node writing that CLAUDE_CODE_EXTRA_BODY), three submitted single-worker runs that declared only the gateway connection (one with forced WebFetch and WebSearch, other-model and background agents, a Workflow, a skill and a compaction, one with a background agent and one with a Workflow meant to outlive the result, each succeeded), and fifteen direct Claude Code runs with native's hosted arguments and environment names, seven against hostile repositories whose settings, agents and skills asked for other models, max effort, more tokens, an extra body, speed fast, the advisor and the web tools, all as 20000:10002 against a scripted model. In it Claude Code contacted only the gateway: one keyless HEAD /api/hello per Claude Code process, then all 163 model calls on claude-opus-5-5 at medium effort with max_tokens 32000, adaptive thinking, no extra body key, no advisor and no 1M-context beta, with the key as x-api-key. No call followed a session's result, no request offered WebFetch, WebSearch or Workflow, each forced call was refused and the turn went on, and Bash, Edit and Write ran. The same harness on dotnet-r5 sent fable, sonnet and haiku subagent calls, max effort with 64000 tokens from an extra body, the advisor tool and calls after the result. The second interrogate panel measured on dotnet-r4, whose hook, MCP and attribution settings dotnet-r6 keeps, that a repository's hooks, .mcp.json server and attribution settings did not apply. Approved accepting that the upstream target image is unattested; that no real Claude Code task has yet run through native and sub2api against GitHub, only those probes and that capture against a scripted model; that Claude Code 2.1.276 logs unrecognized_model for claude-opus-5-5; that a target repository's own .claude/settings.json env entries beyond the pinned keys and its apiKeyHelper still apply (#249); that every command an agent runs, including a repository's build and test code and its dependencies, can read the gateway key, so a nested claude -p from an agent's Bash reaches claude-opus-5, or another model it names, and a direct request can name any model, because the key has no model allowlist (#249); that automatic compaction makes a full-context call at medium effort, by default once each time the context fills, and a repository's env can make it run on most turns (#249); that further settings that raise cost, recorded at https://github.com/faviann/broodling/issues/249#issuecomment-6228140697, are tracked on #249; that native acts on pull-request feedback from anyone who can comment on the pull request; that no spend bound is enforced, because sub2api runs in simple mode, which does not enforce key quotas, so the owner watches spend and that watch is the only bound on the cost of the residuals above (a nested claude -p, a direct request naming any model, a repository's env (#249) and compaction) and of up to 10 iterations with each review retried once (homelab-iac#605); that the key's IP whitelist trusts forwarded headers, so it is advisory, and the gateway is reachable only from the LAN (homelab-iac#605); and that the deployed GH_TOKEN is the owner's own GitHub token, not a fine-grained one, given only to the deliver node, and #253 narrows its scope. Preconditions for every live run, which Broodling does not check: runs are limited to repositories the owner controls whose interactions are limited to collaborators, with the limit renewed before it expires (the canary faviann/broodling-canary's expires on 2027-04-16) or the repository made private (faviann/broodling does not meet this yet, and #253 covers limiting its comments); and GATEWAY_API_KEY is a dedicated sub2api key that only Broodling uses.
